newsitem.title: USA: Officials say not ruling out third bomb in Atlanta.
newsitem.headline: Officials say not ruling out third bomb in Atlanta.

text.p: Federal officials investigating two blasts on Thursday at a building in Atlanta housing an abortion clinic said they could not rule out the possible presence of a third bomb.

"Investigators from state, local and fed agencies are working the scene," said Kent Alexander, U.S. Attorney for the northern district of Georgia, adding that a third device could still be present. "There's no reason to think there is, but there's no reason to think there isn't."
"We're taking every precaution to make sure that if there is another device, that no one gets hurt," Alexander said.

At a news conference, he said officials had not yet determined if the bomb was intended for the abortion clinic on the first floor of the five-story building, which also houses legal, dental and medical offices. "We are not ruling out some other form of domestic terrorism," he said.
A half-dozen emergency officials were treated for minor injuries after the two explosions.

"It is unclear at this point whether it was inside or outside the building," Alexander said of the first explosion, which was followed by another explosion in a garbage bin in the parking lot. "I really can't comment on the nature of the bomb," he said. "Every resource is going to be put toward (investigating) this."
